citation: Federal Acquisition Regulation 32.009-1, Providing accelerated payments to small business contractors and subcontractors: General. acquisition.gov, FAC 2026-01.
population: small business prime contractors and primes with small business subcontractors
effect: agencies shall provide accelerated payments to small business contractors, to the fullest extent permitted by law, with a goal of 15 days after receipt of a proper invoice (31 U.S.C. 3903(a); 10 U.S.C. 3801(b) for DoD), and to primes that agree to pay small business subcontractors within 15 days of receiving the accelerated payment; the acceleration creates no new Prompt Payment Act rights
summary: The cash-flow rule in the firm's favour: a 15-day goal for paying small business primes, against the 30-day Prompt Payment default, which is the gap a biweekly payroll has to bridge when a hire is on the books before the first invoice clears (synthesis).
key_facts: Goal of 15 days for small business contractors; primes pass acceleration to small subcontractors within 15 days
quotes: shall provide accelerated payments, to the fullest extent permitted by law, with a goal of 15 days
role_note: payment timing

tier_note: governing text or official guidance; carried as background because the seminal tier is reserved for the landmark studies the guide rests on (consolidation, 2026-10-22)
citation: 5 CFR § 1315.4, Prompt payment standards and required notices (Prompt Payment Act regulation). Read on law.cornell.edu.
publisher: Office of Management and Budget (Legal Information Institute mirror)
population: federal agencies paying contractors
effect: where the contract sets no date, payment is due 30 days after the start of the payment period, which begins on receipt of a proper invoice (g)(1)(iv), (f); an improper invoice is returned within 7 days (c)(2); interest is paid automatically on late payments (i)
summary: The default clock on getting paid: thirty days from a proper invoice, seven days for the agency to bounce a defective one, interest if late. The reason a hire made against a new task order is paid by the firm for two months before the customer's money arrives (synthesis).
key_facts: 30 days after the payment period starts (receipt of a proper invoice); 7-day return for improper invoices
quotes: 30 days after the start of the payment period as specified in paragraph (f)
role_note: the 30-day payment default

citation: U.S. Government Accountability Office. ASRC Federal Data Solutions, LLC, B-421008; B-421008.2; B-421008.3. Bid protest decision, December 2, 2022.
population: an HHS/NIEHS IT services competition
effect: the bait-and-switch standard: the awardee knowingly or negligently represented it would rely on specific personnel it lacked a reasonable basis to furnish, the agency relied on the representation, and the reliance had a material effect on the evaluation; sustained where a proposed key person had told the awardee she had committed to the protester and could not be used, the quotation nonetheless carried her résumé, the agency credited it with a strength, and an 18.5 percent price premium rested on it; remedy: exclusion, termination of the BPA, a new selection and protest costs
summary: What a tentative opening staffed for a proposal can cost: naming a candidate the firm has no reasonable basis to deliver is a misrepresentation, and when the agency relies on it the award can be unwound. A contingent offer accepted in writing and still standing is the difference between the person GAO accepted and the one it did not.
key_facts: Bait-and-switch: knowing or negligent representation, agency reliance, material effect; protest sustained
A proposed key person who had committed elsewhere and said so could not lawfully be carried in the quotation
quotes: knowingly or negligently represented that it would rely on specific personnel
role_note: proposal staffing representations

citation: Rynes, S. L., Colbert, A. E., & Brown, K. G. (2002). HR professionals' beliefs about effective human resource practices: Correspondence between research and practice. Human Resource Management, 41(2), 149–174.
population: 959 HR professionals responding from 5,000 surveyed
effect: large discrepancies between research findings and practitioner beliefs, largest in selection, where practitioners place far less faith in intelligence and personality tests as predictors of performance than the research supports; agreement higher among senior respondents, SPHR holders and readers of the academic literature
summary: The evidence that staffing conversations run on belief: nearly a thousand HR professionals disagreed with what the selection research had found, most of all on the predictors that matter most. Read from the record; the item-level results are a todo.
key_facts: 959 HR professionals; the largest research–practice gaps in selection
quotes: Responses from 959 participants suggest that there are large discrepancies
role_note: anecdote against evidence

effect: five principles: involve top management, employees and other stakeholders in developing, communicating and implementing the plan; determine the critical skills and competencies needed for current and future results; develop strategies tailored to gaps in number, deployment and alignment; build the capability to support the strategies; monitor and evaluate progress; strategic workforce planning defined as developing long-term strategies for acquiring, developing and retaining the total workforce

quotes: approved by a Government agency such as the Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) within the past 30 months

citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Series ID formats (help page). Accessed October 22, 2026.
population: BLS public data API users
effect: JOLTS series IDs are JT + seasonal code + six-digit industry + two-digit state + five-digit area + two-digit size class + two-character data element (JO, HI, QU, LD, OS) + rate/level (R or L), for example JTU110099000000000HIL; ECI series are CI + seasonal + ownership + component + industry + occupation + subcell + periodicity (CIS1010000000000I); ECEC series are CM + seasonal + ownership + estimate + industry + occupation + subcell + datatype (CMU1010000100000P)
summary: The format behind the refresh routine's series IDs: it confirms the structure of the two JOLTS IDs carried since sweep 2 (JTS540099000000000JOR; JTS000000000000000QUR), with S in the seasonal position for seasonally adjusted series as [235](#cite:235) lists them.
key_facts: JOLTS: JT + S/U + industry + state + area + size + element + R/L
role_note: series ID structure

citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Employment Cost Index series ID guide (factsheet). Accessed October 22, 2026.
population: ECI data users
effect: seventeen-character IDs: CI, S or U, ownership (2 = private industry), estimate (01 total compensation, 02 wages and salaries, 03 benefits), industry 0000, occupation 000, subcell 000, datatype (A = 12-month percent change); wages and salaries for private industry, 12-month change: CIU2020000000000A (not seasonally adjusted) and CIS2020000000000A (seasonally adjusted); total compensation CIU2010000000000A / CIS2010000000000A; benefits CIU2030000000000A / CIS2030000000000A; the page warns that not every combination is published
summary: Confirms the ECI series ID carried on the wage-growth indicator since sweep 3 and supplies the companion IDs for total compensation and benefits; closes the series part of t-3009.
key_facts: CIU2020000000000A is private-industry wages and salaries, 12-month change, not seasonally adjusted
role_note: ECI series IDs

citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Employer Costs for Employee Compensation series ID guide (factsheet). Accessed October 22, 2026.
population: ECEC data users
effect: seventeen-character IDs: CM, U (no seasonally adjusted series), ownership (2 = private industry), estimate (01 total compensation, 02 wages and salaries, 03 benefits), industry, occupation, subcell, datatype (D = cost per hour worked; P = percent of total compensation); total compensation, private industry, all workers: CMU2010000000000D; total benefits: CMU2030000000000D; benefits as a share of compensation: CMU2030000000000P (publication of the combination not confirmed on the page)
summary: The IDs for the benefits-share indicator carried since sweep 3; the percent series is the one the refresh routine should try first, with the two dollar series as the fallback arithmetic.
key_facts: CMU2030000000000P (benefits share) and CMU2010000000000D / CMU2030000000000D (dollars per hour)
role_note: ECEC series IDs

citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OE) time-series documentation (oe.txt). Accessed October 22, 2026.
population: OEWS data users
effect: OEWS series IDs: OE + seasonal (U) + area type (one character) + seven-digit area + six-digit industry + six-digit occupation + two-digit datatype, for example OEUM000040000000000000001; the datatype codes for mean and median wages are in the separate oe.datatype mapping file and are not reproduced in the documentation

role_note: OEWS series ID structure
